claims.text: The baseline RHEA is primarily composed of Nb, Mo, Ta, W, and V.
The baseline RHEA has a solid-solution microstructure.
A minor fraction of nanoscale Y2O3 particles can be incorporated into the RHEA by dispersion-strengthening processing.
The processing intervention will produce a controlled, uniform nanoscale dispersion of oxide particles.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles obstruct dislocation motion.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles obstruct irradiation-induced defect migration.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles stabilize or pin grain boundaries.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles impede irradiation-induced defect coarsening.
Pinning of dislocations and grain boundaries by oxide particles reduces creep.
Oxide-particle pinning delays irradiation-induced microstructural degradation.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will increase the RHEA's yield strength relative to the undoped alloy under otherwise identical high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve ductility relative to the undoped alloy under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve resistance to irradiation-induced defect clustering.
The strengthened RHEA will undergo minimal loss of thermal stability over long exposure periods.
The proposed improvements should hold around 900–1000 °C under irradiation exposure.
Oxide additions used in the proposed regime are typically a few weight percent.
The predicted effects may not persist at substantially higher irradiation doses or temperatures significantly above 1000 °C.
